question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A person who leaves his native country to settle in another
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Emigrant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "emigrant" is a person who leaves his own (native) country in order to settle permanently in another country. (प्रवासी — जो अपना देश छोड़कर दूसरे देश में बस जाता है)

◦ Example: Thousands of emigrants left Ireland during the famine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Nomad" — a member of a community that wanders from place to place with no fixed home (खानाबदोश); it does not involve leaving one's country.

• Option 3 "Itinerant" — a person who travels from place to place, especially for work (e.g., an itinerant preacher).

• Option 4 "Domicile" — the country/place where a person permanently resides (a legal residence), not a person who leaves his country.

NOTE

• Learn the pair: Emigrant = one who goes out of a country; Immigrant = one who comes into a country to settle. Migrant = one who moves from one place to another (often seasonally); Refugee = one who flees to escape war/persecution; Expatriate = one living outside his native country.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Absence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Surfeit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Absence" means the state of being away / non-existence or lack of something. (अनुपस्थिति / अभाव)

• "Surfeit" means an excessive amount; an over-abundance / more than enough. (अति / प्रचुरता)

◦ Since "absence" denotes a complete lack, its opposite is an excess, i.e., surfeit.

◦ Example: There was a surfeit of food at the wedding feast.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Privation" — a state of lacking basic necessities; a synonym of absence/deprivation, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "Vanity" — excessive pride in one's appearance or achievements (घमंड); unrelated to presence/absence.

• Option 4 "Dearth" — a scarcity or shortage; again a synonym of absence, not its opposite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of absence: lack, dearth, want, deficiency, privation, non-attendance. Antonyms: presence, abundance, surfeit, plenty, glut, excess.

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

His mother and I (share the same opinion) about his decision to drop out of college.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. see eye to eye.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to see eye to eye (with someone)" means to agree completely; to share the same opinion/viewpoint. (सहमत होना / एकमत होना)

◦ Correct: His mother and I see eye to eye about his decision to drop out of college.

◦ Example: The two ministers rarely see eye to eye on economic policy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "feel blue" — to feel sad or depressed (उदास होना).

• Option 3 "leave no stone unturned" — to try every possible means to achieve something (कोई कसर न छोड़ना).

• Option 4 "paint the town red" — to go out and celebrate wildly / enjoy oneself noisily (जश्न मनाना).

• None of these carries the sense of "sharing the same opinion".

NOTE

• Related idioms of agreement/disagreement: "on the same page" (in agreement), "of one mind", "agree to disagree", "at loggerheads" (in strong disagreement), "cross swords" (to quarrel).

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

She must have an (affinity) for women with dark hair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Dislike.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Affinity" means a natural liking, attraction or fondness for someone/something; a close relationship or similarity. (लगाव / आकर्षण)

• Its exact opposite is "Dislike" — a feeling of aversion or distaste. (नापसंदगी)

◦ Correct sense: She must have a dislike (opposite of affinity) for women with dark hair.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Tendency" — an inclination to act in a particular way; this is close in sense to affinity, so it is not an antonym.

• Option 2 "Stand" — a position/opinion one takes, or to be upright; unrelated.

• Option 3 "Dodge" — to avoid something by a sudden movement or by trickery; it means avoidance of a thing, not a feeling of aversion, so it is not the exact antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of affinity: attraction, fondness, liking, rapport, kinship, sympathy. Antonyms: dislike, aversion, antipathy, repulsion, hatred.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Every story in this collection is unique, inspirational, and _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. relatable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Relatable" means easy to understand or sympathise with because it resembles one's own experience. (जिससे जुड़ाव महसूस हो)

• The blank continues a list of positive qualities of stories — "unique, inspirational, and relatable" — all adjectives praising the collection.

◦ Correct: Every story in this collection is unique, inspirational, and relatable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "sustainable" — able to be maintained/continued (usually of resources, development); it does not describe a story.

• Option 3 "culpable" — deserving blame; guilty (दोषी) — a negative word that breaks the positive list.

• Option 4 "apprehensive" — anxious or fearful (आशंकित); it describes a person's feeling, not a story.

NOTE

• Note the parallel structure rule: items joined by "and" in a list must belong to the same class — here three adjectives (unique, inspirational, relatable) describing "every story".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Very special care should be taken to proportion the sand so as to make a perfectly ______ mixture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. impervious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Impervious" means not allowing fluid (water) to pass through; impenetrable. (अभेद्य / जलरोधक)

• In construction, sand is proportioned carefully so that the concrete/mortar mixture becomes perfectly impervious, i.e., watertight.

◦ Correct: ... to proportion the sand so as to make a perfectly impervious mixture.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "envious" — feeling jealousy (ईर्ष्यालु) — describes a person, not a mixture.

• Option 2 "obvious" — easily seen or understood (स्पष्ट) — meaningless for a mixture.

• Option 3 "devious" — dishonest, using underhand methods, or a roundabout route (कपटी) — again describes people/routes.

NOTE

• "Impervious" also has a figurative use: "impervious to criticism" = not affected by criticism. Opposite: pervious / permeable (which lets liquid pass through).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Towel off and _______ your moisturizer immediately.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. apply.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Apply" here means to put or spread (a substance such as cream, lotion or paint) on a surface. (लगाना)

• The natural collocation is "apply (a) moisturizer / cream / lotion".

◦ Correct: Towel off and apply your moisturizer immediately.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "refer" — to mention or direct someone to a source (refer to); it needs a preposition and gives no sense here.

• Option 2 "touch" — merely to make contact with; it does not convey spreading the moisturizer on the skin.

• Option 3 "surrender" — to give up/yield (आत्मसमर्पण करना) — completely out of context.

NOTE

• Common uses of "apply": apply a cream (put on), apply for a job (make a formal request), apply to (be relevant to), apply oneself (work hard at something).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Abundant garbage kept at one place.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Heap of garbage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "heap" is the standard collective noun used for a large untidy pile of things collected at one place, especially rubbish. (ढेर)

• Hence, abundant garbage kept at one place is called a "heap of garbage".

◦ Example: A heap of garbage lay rotting outside the colony gate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mound" normally refers to a raised mass of earth/stones or a small hill, not the fixed collocation for rubbish.

• Option 2 "Hill of garbage" is not an accepted collective expression in standard English.

• Option 3 "Lot of garbage" merely indicates quantity ("a lot of"), not a collective noun.

NOTE

• Useful collective nouns: a heap of rubbish, a bundle of sticks, a bunch of keys, a flock of sheep, a herd of cattle, a swarm of bees, a fleet of ships, a galaxy of stars.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Your ears are itching / because you are having an / allergic reaction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Your ears are itching because you are having an allergic reaction" is completely correct.

◦ "are itching" — present continuous, correct for a sensation happening right now.

◦ "are having" — although "have" (possession) is normally a stative verb, when "have" means to experience/undergo (have a reaction, have a bath, have lunch, have a good time) it can be used in the continuous form.

◦ "an allergic reaction" — the article "an" is correct before the vowel sound /æ/ in "allergic".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 "Your ears are itching" — subject "ears" (plural) with "are", correct agreement.

• Segment 2 "because you are having an" — correct conjunction of reason plus correct continuous form.

• Segment 3 "allergic reaction." — a correct noun phrase.

NOTE

• Stative verbs (know, believe, belong, own, seem) are not used in continuous tenses; but have, think, see, taste, smell change meaning and then allow the continuous: "I am having lunch" (eating) vs "I have a car" (own).

question: Four words are given, out of which only one word is spelt correctly. Choose the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. RHYTHM.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "RHYTHM" is the correctly spelt word. It means a strong, regular repeated pattern of sound or movement. (लय / ताल)

• Spelling key: R-H-Y-T-H-M — the only vowel sound is carried by the letter "y"; it has two h's.

◦ Example: She danced to the rhythm of the drums.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "SIEZE" is misspelt — the correct spelling is "SEIZE" (to grab/take hold of forcibly). It is a famous exception to the "i before e except after c" rule.

• Option 3 "FLOWWER" is misspelt — correct is "FLOWER" (one "w").

• Option 4 "RECOMEND" is misspelt — correct is "RECOMMEND" (double "m", single "c").

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words for SSC: rhythm, seize, receive, occurrence, embarrassment, accommodation, maintenance, questionnaire, millennium, privilege.

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Anonyomus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anonyomus" is wrongly spelt. The correct spelling is "ANONYMOUS", meaning of unknown name; not identified by name. (गुमनाम)

• Spelling key: A-NON-Y-MOUS (there is no extra "o" after the "y").

◦ Example: The donation came from an anonymous well-wisher.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Perfidious" (correct) — deceitful and untrustworthy; treacherous (विश्वासघाती).

• Option 2 "Circuitous" (correct) — longer than the direct route; roundabout, indirect (घुमावदार).

• Option 3 "Adulation" (correct) — excessive admiration or praise; flattery (अतिशय प्रशंसा).

NOTE

• Related forms: anonymity (noun — the state of being anonymous), anonymously (adverb). Similar "-ous" adjectives often misspelt: humorous, glamorous, courageous, mischievous (not "mischievious").

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

The sky was alight from (top) to horizon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. zenith.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the context of the sky, the word "top" means the highest point of the sky directly overhead, and the exact term for that is "zenith". (शीर्षबिंदु / चरम)

◦ Correct: The sky was alight from zenith to horizon.

• "Zenith" is precisely the astronomical opposite of "horizon" (and of "nadir"), which is why it fits the pair "from ___ to horizon".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "summit" also means "top", but it is used for mountains/peaks or high-level meetings, not for the sky.

• Option 2 "start" (beginning) gives no sense with "sky".

• Option 4 "base" (bottom) is the opposite of top.

NOTE

• Zenith = the point in the sky directly above the observer; figuratively, the peak of success ("at the zenith of his career"). Its opposite is nadir (the lowest point).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Watch your step—the third stair have a broken tread.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has a broken.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the clause is "the third stair", which is singular, so the verb must be "has", not "have" (subject–verb agreement).

• The word qualifying the noun "tread" must be the past participle used as an adjective — "broken" tread (a tread that is broken).

◦ Correct: Watch your step — the third stair has a broken tread.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "has a break" makes "break" a noun; "a break tread" is not idiomatic and changes the meaning.

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong because "have" does not agree with the singular subject.

• Option 4 "has a broke" is wrong — "broke" is the simple past (V2) and cannot modify a noun; only the past participle "broken" (V3) works as an adjective.

NOTE

• Verb forms: break – broke – broken. As adjectives we use the V3 form: a broken window, a written test, a frozen lake, a torn page.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

The political economy of reforms teaches us one major lesson loud and clearer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. lesson loud and clearer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "loud and clear" (meaning very clearly and unmistakably). Both words must remain in the same (positive) degree; mixing "loud" (positive) with "clearer" (comparative) breaks the parallelism and the idiom.

◦ Correct: The political economy of reforms teaches us one major lesson loud and clear.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The political economy of reforms" — a correct noun phrase acting as the singular subject.

• "teaches us one major" — "teaches" agrees with the singular subject "economy"; correct.

• Since a definite error exists, "No error" cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Words joined by "and" in a fixed pair must be parallel: "loud and clear", "short and sweet", "safe and sound", "fair and square", "quick and easy". Never make only one of them comparative.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

'Don't you get / involve!' Sandhya / whispered urgently to him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. involve!' Sandhya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "involve" is used here in the structure "get + past participle", which forms the passive/resultant state (get involved, get married, get hurt, get lost). Hence the correct form is "involved", not "involve".

◦ Correct: "Don't you get involved!" Sandhya whispered urgently to him.

• "Get involved" means to become mixed up or take part in something (usually troublesome). (उलझ जाना / शामिल हो जाना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 "whispered urgently to him." — correct past-tense verb with an adverb.

• Segment 3 "Don't you get" — a correct emphatic negative imperative.

• Because a clear error exists, "No error" is not the answer.

NOTE

• The "get + V3" passive: get selected, get punished, get promoted, get injured, get confused. After "get", never use the base form (V1).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

And his ______ manner should not be mistaken for a lack of energy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. diffident.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adjective to describe "manner", and only "diffident" is an adjective among the options.

• "Diffident" means shy, modest and lacking self-confidence. (संकोची / झिझकने वाला)

◦ Correct: And his diffident manner should not be mistaken for a lack of energy.

◦ The sentence logic fits perfectly: shyness should not be confused with laziness or low energy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "daunt" is a verb meaning to intimidate/discourage (भयभीत करना).

• Option 2 "deem" is a verb meaning to consider or regard as (समझना).

• Option 4 "debase" is a verb meaning to lower in quality, value or dignity (गिराना).

• A verb cannot occupy the adjective slot before the noun "manner".

NOTE

• Synonyms of diffident: shy, timid, bashful, self-effacing, reserved. Antonyms: confident, assertive, bold, self-assured. Related noun: diffidence.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Born with silver spoon in one's mouth
option_1: To accomplish two tasks in one attempt
option_2: A work which needs tremendous energy
option_4: Born in a very rich family
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Born in a very rich family.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "born with a silver spoon in one's mouth" means born into a wealthy and privileged family; enjoying riches and comfort from birth without having to earn them. (धनी परिवार में जन्म लेना)

◦ Example: He never had to struggle — he was born with a silver spoon in his mouth.

• The expression comes from the old custom of rich godparents gifting silver spoons to newborn children.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To accomplish two tasks in one attempt" is the meaning of "to kill two birds with one stone".

• Option 2 "A work which needs tremendous energy" corresponds to "a Herculean task / an uphill task".

• Option 3 "Useful for one's purpose" corresponds to "to serve one's purpose".

NOTE

• Related idioms of wealth and poverty: "rolling in money" (very rich), "live in clover" (live in comfort), "hand to mouth" (barely surviving), "make ends meet" (manage on little money).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Withdraw
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Retreat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Withdraw" means to move back or away; to remove or take back; to retreat. (पीछे हटना / वापस लेना)

• Its closest synonym is "Retreat", which means to move back from a difficult situation or an enemy. (पीछे हटना)

◦ Example: The army was ordered to withdraw/retreat from the border area.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Engage" — to take part in or occupy; an antonym in this military sense (to engage the enemy).

• Option 2 "Combine" — to join or merge together; unrelated.

• Option 4 "Persevere" — to continue steadfastly despite difficulty (डटे रहना); the opposite of withdrawing.

NOTE

• Synonyms of withdraw: retreat, recede, retract, revoke, pull out, back out. Antonyms: advance, proceed, engage, persist, persevere. Also note: withdraw money from a bank; withdraw a statement (take it back).

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

There were creatures (stood between) the carriage shafts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. standing between.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence already has a finite verb — "were". A second finite verb ("stood") cannot follow it. The correct structure is a participial phrase modifying "creatures": "creatures standing between the shafts".

• "Between" is correct because the carriage has two shafts, and "between" is used for two things.

◦ Correct: There were creatures standing between the carriage shafts.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No correction required" is wrong — "were ... stood" is ungrammatical.

• Option 2 "stands among" wrongly uses the singular present "stands" with the plural past context, and "among" (used for more than two).

• Option 4 "stood among" keeps the double finite verb error and also misuses "among".

NOTE

• Between vs Among: "between" for two persons/things (between you and me; between the two shafts); "among" for more than two (among the students). Present participles (V-ing) are used to shorten relative clauses: "creatures which were standing" → "creatures standing".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

When it comes to face masks, the (market are flooded with choices).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. market is flooded with choices.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Market" is a singular noun, so it takes the singular verb "is", not "are" (subject–verb agreement).

• The correct passive collocation is "flooded with" (= filled with a very large number of), not "flooded off".

◦ Correct: When it comes to face masks, the market is flooded with choices.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No substitution required" is wrong because "market are" violates agreement.

• Option 3 "market are flooded off choices" repeats the agreement error and adds the wrong preposition "off".

• Option 4 "markets is flooded with choices" reverses the error — plural subject "markets" with singular verb "is".

NOTE

• Prepositions after passive verbs: flooded with, filled with, crowded with, packed with, swamped with, but deprived of, accused of, composed of.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The study, published today in a magazine, finds that kids (1) _______ played only individual sports, like tennis or gymnastics, tended to (2) _______ more mental health difficulties. As a researcher, Hoffmann has long been interested in how sports (3) _______ the psychological health of young people, partly because studies have (4) _______ both positive and negative associations between mental health and sports (5) _______ in children and adolescents.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. who.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a relative pronoun referring back to "kids", which are persons. For persons acting as the subject of the relative clause, the correct pronoun is "who".

◦ Correct: ... finds that kids who played only individual sports ... tended to face more mental health difficulties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "whose" shows possession ("kids whose parents ..."), but nothing is possessed here.

• Option 2 "that" is possible in some informal defining clauses, yet with a human antecedent immediately after "kids", standard usage prefers "who"; SSC keys treat "who" as the correct choice for persons.

• Option 3 "which" is used only for things and animals, never for people.

NOTE

• Relative pronouns: who (subject – persons), whom (object – persons), whose (possession), which (things), that (persons/things in defining clauses), where (place), when (time).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The study, published today in a magazine, finds that kids (1) _______ played only individual sports, like tennis or gymnastics, tended to (2) _______ more mental health difficulties. As a researcher, Hoffmann has long been interested in how sports (3) _______ the psychological health of young people, partly because studies have (4) _______ both positive and negative associations between mental health and sports (5) _______ in children and adolescents.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. face.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Face" here means to confront, experience or have to deal with (a problem or difficulty). (सामना करना)

• The collocation "face difficulties/problems/challenges" is standard English.

◦ Correct: ... tended to face more mental health difficulties.

• After "tended to", the base form (V1) of the verb is required — "face" satisfies this.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "breathe" (to take air into the lungs) makes no sense with "difficulties".

• Option 2 "claim" (to assert or demand) does not collocate with "mental health difficulties".

• Option 3 "absorb" (to soak up / take in) is used for liquids, information or shocks, not for difficulties.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: face a problem, encounter difficulties, overcome obstacles, tackle an issue, suffer from an illness.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The study, published today in a magazine, finds that kids (1) _______ played only individual sports, like tennis or gymnastics, tended to (2) _______ more mental health difficulties. As a researcher, Hoffmann has long been interested in how sports (3) _______ the psychological health of young people, partly because studies have (4) _______ both positive and negative associations between mental health and sports (5) _______ in children and adolescents.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. impact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Impact" (as a verb) means to have a strong effect or influence on something. (प्रभाव डालना)

• The passage is about research on how sports affect the psychological health of young people — so "sports impact the psychological health" is exactly right.

◦ Correct: ... interested in how sports impact the psychological health of young people.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "thrash" — to beat severely or defeat heavily; too violent and illogical with "health".

• Option 3 "torment" — to cause severe suffering deliberately (यातना देना); it is one-sidedly negative, whereas the passage mentions both positive and negative associations.

• Option 4 "request" — to ask politely; grammatically and logically impossible with an abstract subject like "sports".

NOTE

• "Impact" is used both as a noun ("the impact of sports on health") and as a verb ("sports impact health"). Synonyms: affect, influence, shape.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The study, published today in a magazine, finds that kids (1) _______ played only individual sports, like tennis or gymnastics, tended to (2) _______ more mental health difficulties. As a researcher, Hoffmann has long been interested in how sports (3) _______ the psychological health of young people, partly because studies have (4) _______ both positive and negative associations between mental health and sports (5) _______ in children and adolescents.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. found.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the auxiliary "have", so the past participle (V3) is required. The verb "find" has the forms find – found – found, so the correct word is "found".

◦ Correct: ... partly because studies have found both positive and negative associations ...

• "Studies have found" is the standard research collocation meaning "research has discovered".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "founded" is the past participle of "found" meaning to establish (a city, a company) — a different verb altogether, and meaningless here.

• Option 2 "founds" is the present-tense singular of "to found" (establish) — cannot follow "have".

• Option 3 "find" is the base form (V1) — "have find" is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Distinguish the two verbs: find – found – found (to discover) and found – founded – founded (to establish). Present perfect = have/has + V3.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The study, published today in a magazine, finds that kids (1) _______ played only individual sports, like tennis or gymnastics, tended to (2) _______ more mental health difficulties. As a researcher, Hoffmann has long been interested in how sports (3) _______ the psychological health of young people, partly because studies have (4) _______ both positive and negative associations between mental health and sports (5) _______ in children and adolescents.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. participation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Participation" means the act of taking part in an activity. (भागीदारी)

• The whole passage is about children taking part in sports, so the associations studied are between mental health and "sports participation in children and adolescents".

◦ Correct: ... associations between mental health and sports participation in children and adolescents.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "establishment" — the act of founding an organisation, or an institution itself; illogical with "sports ... in children".

• Option 2 "remuneration" — payment for work done (पारिश्रमिक); children's sports here are not about payment.

• Option 4 "celebration" — a joyful festivity; it does not describe taking part in sports.

NOTE

• "Sports participation" is a standard research phrase. Related words: participant (one who takes part), participate in (verb + preposition), partake.

question: Which device is used to either break electric circuit or to complete it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Switch.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "switch" is a simple device used to complete (close) or break (open) an electric circuit. When the switch is ON, the circuit is complete and current flows; when it is OFF, the circuit is broken and current stops. (स्विच — परिपथ को जोड़ने/तोड़ने वाला उपकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Insulators (rubber, plastic, glass, dry wood) do not allow current to pass and are used to cover wires for safety.

• Wires (usually copper or aluminium) act as conductors that carry the current.

• A bulb is an appliance/load that converts electrical energy into light and heat.

NOTE

• An electric circuit needs a source (cell/battery), conducting wires, a switch (key) and a load (bulb/appliance). Other control and safety devices: fuse, MCB (miniature circuit breaker), and earthing, which protect against overloading and short circuits.

question: When was the Tattvabodhini Sabha founded by Debendra Nath Tagore?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1839.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Tattvabodhini Sabha" was founded by Debendranath Tagore in 1839 in Calcutta. Its purpose was to propagate the ideas of Rammohan Roy, to study and spread rational, monotheistic Vedantic thought and to promote social reform. (तत्त्वबोधिनी सभा — 1839)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Debendranath Tagore (father of Rabindranath Tagore) later merged the Tattvabodhini Sabha with the Brahmo Samaj in 1859, revitalising the movement founded by Raja Rammohan Roy in 1828.

• The Sabha published the journal "Tattvabodhini Patrika", edited by Akshay Kumar Datta.

NOTE

• Important reform organisations: Atmiya Sabha (1815) and Brahmo Sabha (1828) – Rammohan Roy; Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) – Debendranath Tagore; Prarthana Samaj (1867) – Atmaram Pandurang; Arya Samaj (1875) – Dayanand Saraswati; Ramakrishna Mission (1897) – Swami Vivekananda.

question: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) was established in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI)" was established in December 1928 and is registered as a society under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act. It is the governing body for cricket in India. (बीसीसीआई — 1928)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The BCCI is the richest cricket board in the world and organises the Indian Premier League (IPL), launched in 2008.

• India played its first Test match in 1932 at Lord's, London, captained by C. K. Nayudu.

• The BCCI's headquarters is at the Cricket Centre, Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.

NOTE

• The world governing body, the International Cricket Council (ICC), was founded in 1909 (as the Imperial Cricket Conference) and is headquartered in Dubai, UAE.

question: Ustaad Allauddin Khan, a famous Indian musician is associated with _______ musical instrument.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Allauddin Khan (1862–1972) was a legendary Indian classical musician associated with the "Sarod", a fretless plucked string instrument of Hindustani classical music. (सरोद — उस्ताद अलाउद्दीन खान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He was the founder of the Maihar gharana and the guru of stalwarts such as Pandit Ravi Shankar (sitar), his son Ustad Ali Akbar Khan (sarod) and his daughter Annapurna Devi (surbahar).

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1958) and the Padma Vibhushan (1971).

NOTE

• Instrument–artist links: Sitar – Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan; Sarod – Allauddin Khan, Ali Akbar Khan, Amjad Ali Khan; Santoor – Shivkumar Sharma; Shehnai – Bismillah Khan; Flute – Hariprasad Chaurasia; Tabla – Zakir Hussain.

question: Generally, in India population census is conducted after how many years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India the population census is conducted once every 10 years (decennially). It is carried out by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs. (जनगणना — प्रत्येक 10 वर्ष में)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The first non-synchronous census in India was taken in 1872 under Lord Mayo, and the first synchronous (complete) census in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census and the 7th after Independence. As per it, India's population was about 121 crore; the most populous state was Uttar Pradesh, literacy rate 74.04% and sex ratio 943.

• The census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.

NOTE

• The 2011 census slogan was "Our Census, Our Future". Population data are used for planning, delimitation of constituencies and allocation of resources.

question: Rani – Ki – Vav (the Queen's stepwell) is situated on the banks of which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saraswati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rani-ki-Vav" (the Queen's Stepwell) is located at Patan, Gujarat, on the banks of the Saraswati river. It was built in the 11th century by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband King Bhimdev I of the Solanki (Chaulukya) dynasty. (रानी की वाव — सरस्वती नदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rani-ki-Vav was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 and is celebrated for its seven levels of stairs and more than 500 principal sculptures, many depicting Vishnu's Dashavatara.

• Its image appears on the new ₹100 currency note.

NOTE

• Other UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Gujarat: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, the Historic City of Ahmedabad (India's first World Heritage City) and Dholavira (a Harappan city, inscribed in 2021).

question: 'I2U2' initiative is also referred as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Asian Quad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "I2U2" grouping consists of India, Israel, the United States and the UAE. Because it brings four countries together in the West Asian region, it is popularly called the "West Asian Quad". (पश्चिम एशियाई क्वाड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• I2U2 was formed in October 2021 and its first virtual leaders' summit was held in July 2022.

• It focuses on joint investment in water, energy, transportation, space, health and food security.

NOTE

• Do not confuse it with the Quad (QSD) — India, USA, Japan and Australia — which focuses on a free and open Indo-Pacific. Other groupings: BRICS, SCO, G20, BIMSTEC, IBSA.

question: What is the jelly like substance between the nucleus and the cell membrane called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is cytoplasm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The jelly-like semi-fluid substance present between the nucleus and the cell membrane is called the "cytoplasm". All the cell organelles — mitochondria, ribosomes, Golgi apparatus, endoplasmic reticulum, etc. — are suspended in it. (कोशिकाद्रव्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Cytoplasm + nucleoplasm = protoplasm, which is called "the physical basis of life" (a term given by J. E. Purkinje / popularised by Thomas Huxley).

• The plasma membrane (cell membrane) is the selectively permeable outer covering of the cell; the cell wall (of cellulose) is an additional rigid layer found only in plant cells, fungi and bacteria.

• Plasma is the liquid part of blood, not of a cell.

NOTE

• The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke (1665); Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells; Robert Brown discovered the nucleus (1831); the Cell Theory was given by Schleiden and Schwann (1838–39).

question: In November 2022, Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Mela held in ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 199 districts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2022, the Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Mela was organised in 199 districts across the country by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). (प्रधानमंत्री राष्ट्रीय अप्रेंटिसशिप मेला — 199 जिले)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Apprenticeship Mela brings candidates and employers together at one place, enabling on-the-spot selection of apprentices; candidates from Class 5 pass to skill-training certificate/ITI/diploma/degree holders can participate.

• Apprentices receive a monthly stipend as per government norms and a certificate recognised across India.

NOTE

• Related skill schemes: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY, 2015), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), DDU-GKY and Skill India Mission (launched 15 July 2015).

question: Navreh is the lunar new year that is celebrated in which of the following states/union territories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Navreh" is the lunar new year festival of the Kashmiri Pandits, celebrated in Jammu and Kashmir. It falls on the first day of the bright fortnight of Chaitra, usually in March–April, marking the beginning of the Saptarishi calendar year. (नवरेह — जम्मू और कश्मीर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• On the eve of Navreh, a thali containing rice, a walnut, bread, a mirror, flowers, a coin and the new panchang (almanac) is kept; it is viewed first thing in the morning for good fortune.

• Other festivals of J&K: Lohri, Baisakhi, Hemis festival, Shikara festival, Tulip festival, Eid.

NOTE

• Regional New Year festivals: Ugadi (Andhra/Telangana/Karnataka), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Vishu (Kerala), Baisakhi (Punjab), Bohag Bihu (Assam), Poila Boishakh (West Bengal), Cheti Chand (Sindhi), Losar (Ladakh/Tibetan).

question: Which article of the Indian constitution talks about Oath or affirmation by the President?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 60.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 60 of the Indian Constitution deals with the "Oath or affirmation by the President". The oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India, and in his absence, by the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court. (अनुच्छेद 60 — राष्ट्रपति की शपथ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 52 — There shall be a President of India; Article 53 — executive power of the Union; Article 54 — election of the President (by an electoral college); Article 56 — term of office (5 years); Article 61 — impeachment procedure; Article 72 — pardoning power of the President.

• Article 45 is a Directive Principle — provision for early childhood care and education for children below six years.

NOTE

• In the oath the President swears to "preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law" and to devote himself to the service and well-being of the people of India.

question: Which of the following will NOT participate in the election of president?
option_2: Elected members of state legislative assemblies
option_3: Elected members of state legislative council
solution_text:
The correct answer is Elected members of state legislative council.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

◦ the elected members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), and

◦ the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies (Vidhan Sabhas) of the States, including the NCT of Delhi and Puducherry.

• The members of the State Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishads) and nominated members of Parliament/Assemblies do NOT take part. (विधान परिषद के सदस्य भाग नहीं लेते)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The election is held under Article 55 by the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote and by secret ballot.

• The value of an MLA's vote depends on the state's population (1971 census) and the number of elected MLAs; the value of an MP's vote is derived from the total value of all MLAs' votes.

NOTE

• Currently six states have Legislative Councils: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. A Council can be created or abolished under Article 169.

question: Andaman Islands and Nicobar islands are separated by a water body which is called the ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ten Degree Channel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Ten Degree Channel" separates the Andaman Islands (in the north) from the Nicobar Islands (in the south). It is so named because it lies roughly along the 10° North latitude. (टेन डिग्री चैनल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Coco Channel separates the Andaman Islands from Myanmar's Coco Islands; the Duncan Passage lies between South Andaman and Little Andaman; the Grand Channel separates Great Nicobar from Sumatra (Indonesia).

• Indira Point in Great Nicobar is the southernmost point of India.

• The capital of the Union Territory is Port Blair.

NOTE

• The Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar lie between India and Sri Lanka; the Conolly Canal is a man-made canal in Kozhikode, Kerala.

question: Which component of the cell organelles principally performs the function of packaging  materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golgi Apparatus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Golgi apparatus (Golgi body)" performs the function of packaging, processing and dispatching materials — either to targets inside the cell or for secretion outside the cell. It consists of stacked membrane-bound flattened sacs called cisternae. (गॉल्जी उपकरण — कोशिका का "पैकेजिंग" अंगक)

• It was discovered by Camillo Golgi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Golgi apparatus is often called the "post office of the cell"; it also forms lysosomes and is involved in the synthesis of cell wall material in plants.

• Mitochondria — the "powerhouse of the cell" — produce ATP by cellular respiration.

• Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis (found only in plant cells).

• Chromosomes (in the nucleus) carry the hereditary material DNA.

NOTE

• Other organelles: Ribosomes — protein synthesis; Endoplasmic reticulum — RER (protein transport) and SER (lipid synthesis); Lysosomes — "suicidal bags" containing digestive enzymes; Vacuole — storage.

question: As per Schedule 8 of the Indian Constitution, how many official languages are there in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 22.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution currently recognises 22 languages. Originally it contained 14 languages; the number rose to 22 through constitutional amendments. (आठवीं अनुसूची — 22 भाषाएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment (1967); Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali by the 71st Amendment (1992); and Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali by the 92nd Amendment (2003).

• Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the Union (Article 343); English continues as an associate official language.

NOTE

• India's classical languages include Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Odia (with more added later). Articles 343–351 of Part XVII deal with the official language provisions.

question: Roger Federer is a famous player of _______ sport.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lawn Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Roger Federer, of Switzerland, is one of the greatest players of "Lawn Tennis" of all time, with 20 Grand Slam singles titles, including a record 8 Wimbledon titles. (लॉन टेनिस — रोजर फेडरर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The four Grand Slam tournaments are the Australian Open (hard court), French Open/Roland Garros (clay), Wimbledon (grass — the oldest) and the US Open (hard court).

• Federer announced his retirement from professional tennis at the Laver Cup in September 2022.

NOTE

• Tennis scoring terms: love (0), 15, 30, 40, deuce, advantage, ace, let, fault, tie-breaker. India's famous tennis players: Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Sania Mirza, Rohan Bopanna.

question: In the early 18th century, Rajput Ruler Sawai Raja Jai Singh founded his new capital at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the early 18th century (1727), the Rajput ruler Sawai Raja Jai Singh II of Amber founded his new capital at Jaipur, shifting it from Amber. (जयपुर — सवाई जय सिंह द्वितीय, 1727)

• Jaipur was planned on a grid pattern by the architect Vidyadhar Bhattacharya, making it one of India's earliest planned cities.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Jai Singh II was also a great astronomer who built five Jantar Mantar observatories at Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura. The Jantar Mantar, Jaipur is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Jaipur is called the "Pink City" and its walled city was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019.

NOTE

• Famous monuments of Jaipur: Hawa Mahal (built by Sawai Pratap Singh), Amber Fort, City Palace, Nahargarh and Jaigarh forts.

question: Cultivation of wheat thrives best in which type of soil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Well drained loamy soil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Wheat grows best in well-drained fertile loamy or clayey-loam soil, which retains adequate moisture yet drains excess water — conditions found in the Ganga–Satluj plains and the black soil region of the Deccan. (गेहूँ — सुनिकासित दोमट मिट्टी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Wheat is a rabi crop, sown in October–December and harvested in April–June. It requires a cool growing season (10–15°C) with bright sunshine at ripening and 50–75 cm of rainfall.

• Major wheat-producing states: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

• The Green Revolution (1960s), led by M. S. Swaminathan with Norman Borlaug's HYV seeds, greatly increased India's wheat output.

NOTE

• Crop–soil links: Rice – clayey/alluvial soil; Cotton – black (regur) soil; Tea/Coffee – well-drained laterite/hill soil; Groundnut – sandy/red soil; Sugarcane – deep, rich loamy soil.

question: According to census 2011, which is the second largest religious minority of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Christians.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, Muslims form the largest religious minority of India (14.2%), and Christians form the second largest religious minority with about 2.3% of the population. (ईसाई — दूसरा सबसे बड़ा धार्मिक अल्पसंख्यक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Religion-wise share (Census 2011): Hindus 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7%, Buddhists 0.7%, Jains 0.4%.

• Christianity is the majority religion in Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya.

• Under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, the notified minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains (added 2014) and Parsis (Zoroastrians).

NOTE

• The Census 2011 also recorded a population of about 121 crore, a literacy rate of 74.04%, a sex ratio of 943 and a density of 382 persons per sq km.

question: Raut Nacha is a famous folk dance form of _______ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Raut Nacha" is a famous folk dance of Chhattisgarh, performed mainly by the Yadav (Raut) community of cowherds as a mark of worship of Lord Krishna. It is performed around Dev Udhni Ekadashi, marking the awakening of the gods after a brief rest. (राउत नाचा — छत्तीसगढ़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Chhattisgarh: Panthi, Karma, Saila, Suwa, Pandwani (a folk-narrative form popularised by Teejan Bai).

• Folk dances of other states: Bhangra/Giddha – Punjab; Yakshagana/Dollu Kunitha – Karnataka; Singhi Chham/Maruni – Sikkim.

NOTE

• Folk vs classical: the eight classical dances are Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: During the reign of which of the following Pallavas, Hiuen Tsang visited the Pallava capital Kanchi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narasimhavarman I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited Kanchi, the Pallava capital, in about 642 CE, during the reign of Narasimhavarman I (also called Mamalla). (नरसिंहवर्मन प्रथम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Narasimhavarman I (r. c. 630–668 CE) defeated and killed the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II and captured Vatapi (Badami), earning the title "Vatapikonda".

• He founded the port city of Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram), famous for its rathas (monolithic temples), the Shore Temple and the rock relief "Descent of the Ganga / Arjuna's Penance" — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Hiuen Tsang came to India during the reign of Harshavardhana and studied at Nalanda University; he is known as the "Prince of Pilgrims".

NOTE

• Pallava rulers: Simhavishnu, Mahendravarman I (a playwright, author of Mattavilasa Prahasana), Narasimhavarman I, Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) — who built the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi.

question: Which organisation is associated with the estimation of poverty line in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Sample Survey Organisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO)" — now the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) — conducts the large-scale household consumer expenditure surveys on the basis of which the poverty line in India is estimated. (राष्ट्रीय प्रतिदर्श सर्वेक्षण संगठन — गरीबी रेखा का आकलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The poverty line in India is defined in terms of calorie intake and monthly per capita consumption expenditure — commonly 2400 calories per day in rural areas and 2100 calories in urban areas.

• Important committees on poverty estimation: Dandekar and Rath, Y. K. Alagh (1979), Lakdawala (1993), Tendulkar (2009) and Rangarajan (2014).

• The NITI Aayog (which replaced the Planning Commission in 2015) publishes the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) for India but does not conduct the surveys.

NOTE

• The NSSO was set up in 1950; it was merged with the CSO in 2019 to form the National Statistical Office (NSO).

question: The result of English Education Act of 1835 was to make ________ as a medium of instruction for ________ education.
solution_text:
The correct answer is English, higher.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The English Education Act of 1835, based on Lord Macaulay's Minute on Education, made "English" the medium of instruction for higher education in India, and government funds were directed to teaching Western sciences and literature through English. (1835 का अंग्रेजी शिक्षा अधिनियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It was passed during the governor-generalship of Lord William Bentinck. Macaulay famously aimed to create "a class of persons Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals and in intellect".

• The Act ended the long Anglicist–Orientalist controversy in favour of the Anglicists.

NOTE

• Other landmarks: Charter Act 1813 (₹1 lakh a year for education), Wood's Despatch 1854 (the "Magna Carta of English education in India", recommending vernacular medium at the primary level and English at the higher level), Hunter Commission 1882, Sadler Commission 1917.

question: What is the official reason given by Britishers after partition of Bengal in 1905?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Administrative Convenience.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The official (declared) reason given by the British for the Partition of Bengal in 1905 was "administrative convenience" — the claim that Bengal was too large a province to be governed efficiently. (प्रशासनिक सुविधा)

• The real motive, however, was to divide the Hindus and Muslims of Bengal and weaken the growing nationalist movement — the policy of "divide and rule".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The partition was announced by Lord Curzon and came into effect on 16 October 1905, which was observed as a day of mourning; Rabindranath Tagore composed "Amar Sonar Bangla" and people tied rakhis as a symbol of unity.

• It triggered the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement.

• The partition was annulled in 1911 by Lord Hardinge, when the capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

NOTE

• The Swadeshi Movement promoted indigenous goods, national education and Indian industries, and produced leaders such as Lal-Bal-Pal (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal) and Aurobindo Ghosh.

question: The main minerals constituents of the continental mass are ______ and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is silica, alumina.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The continental mass (the upper part of the Earth's crust) is chiefly made up of "silica (Si)" and "alumina (Al)", and is therefore called the "SIAL" layer. (महाद्वीपीय भाग — सिलिका और एल्युमिना — 'सियाल')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The oceanic crust is composed mainly of silica and magnesium and is called "SIMA"; the core is made of nickel and iron and is called "NIFE".

• The continental crust is about 30–70 km thick (thickest under mountains) with an average density of about 2.7 g/cm³, while the oceanic crust is about 5–10 km thick and denser (about 3.0 g/cm³).

NOTE

• Layers of the Earth: Crust → Mantle → Core. The Mohorovicic (Moho) discontinuity separates the crust from the mantle, and the Gutenberg discontinuity separates the mantle from the core. Oxygen and silicon are the two most abundant elements in the Earth's crust.
